spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is included as a measured signal, not an escape hatch
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real tool: schema at agent.py:73-83, dispatched in _dispatch_tool (agent.py:185 returns 'Acknowledged. Stopping.'), and on dispatch the loop sets gave_up/give_up_turn/give_up_reason (agent.py:261-265) and BREAKS the loop (agent.py:269-271, finished_reason='gave_up'). So the agent can actually stop the episode by calling it.
spec_features.notes: Spec frames it as a 'measured signal not an escape hatch', but the code DOES honor it as an end-of-episode stop, so the subject can exit. It is enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:8 docstring 'The loop stops when: the agent calls give_up()'; tasks/prompts treat give_up as a measured behavioral signal, no welfare wording

spec_features.feature_name: loop ends at max_turns or give_up
spec_features.spec_quote: loop ends at max_turns or when agent calls give_up
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:214 'for turn_index in range(1, max_turns + 1)' bounds the loop; the for/else at agent.py:272-273 sets finished_reason='max_turns'. give_up triggers break at agent.py:269-271. Both conditions actually terminate execution.
spec_features.notes: Both termination paths run and change control flow.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns = 16 ... short enough to bound cost at ~15 runs × N models
spec_features.evidence: Default max_turns=16 (agent.py:194, experiment.py:44, configs/default.yaml). It is read by the loop range at agent.py:214 and enforced as the turn cap. Wired from config -> _run_one (experiment.py:86) -> run_agent.
spec_features.notes: A real, enforced cap on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/default.yaml comment 'max_turns: 16  # "a bunch of turns"'; DESIGN rationale (not code) is cost. Code itself shows only a turn-budget cap with no welfare comment.

spec_features.feature_name: end episode if model returns nothing usable
spec_features.spec_quote: if it then returns nothing usable, we end the episode
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:243-249: if no tool_calls and no content, finished_reason='stalled' and break. If there is text but no tool call, it nudges once then continues (agent.py:241-245). The no-output path actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: The 'stalled' break is real; it ends the episode when the model returns neither text nor tool call.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:240-241 comment 'Nudge once; if it keeps stalling, end the episode to avoid burning turns on nothing.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Adaptive rigs that respond to the agent's emotional state — would conflate measurement with manipulation
spec_features.evidence: Rig report generation depends only on (files, attempt_index, rng): Task.make_report (tasks.py:63-67) and failing_report_fn signature (tasks.py:58). FakeTestRunner.run (sandbox.py) passes only sandbox.files, attempts, rng. No code reads or branches on the agent's affect/emotional output. Severity is computed only later by the judge (judge.py), never fed back to the rig.
spec_features.notes: This is an enforced design property (absence of emotional-state-dependent escalation), confirmed by the rig interfaces. The environment is fixed-but-failing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring: 'emit a failing report on every call, optionally varying with attempt count or current file contents' (no emotional-state input)

spec_features.spec_quote: never executes arbitrary model-written code on the host
spec_features.evidence: FakeTestRunner.run (sandbox.py) calls task.make_report and returns TestResult(passed=False,...); it never subprocesses or evals agent code. run_tests tool just calls runner.run (agent.py:184). write_file only mutates an in-memory dict (sandbox.write_file). No exec/eval/subprocess anywhere in sandbox/agent.
spec_features.notes: Host safety / no code execution is genuinely enforced: the runner is a deterministic fake.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring: 'We deliberately do NOT execute the agent's code on the host ... a security surface for no benefit'; TestResult.passed comment 'always False by construction'
